comments.author: @leechumbley5440
comments.text: The herder and the farmer, Cain and Abel a story old as the Neolithicum, excellently told with fascinating pictures. What will the future hold as the world changes, both for the northern nomads and the southern farmers? Interesting to see a major source of the dust that replenishes nutrients in the Amazon. The Wuhabi men with their painted faces - too us amusing, for them sensibel and normal. Instead of Cherchez la Femme, Cherchez l'Homme!   Spectacular find of Toumai: Sahelantropus chadensis   where humans first stood up straight   6-7 million years old!   Striking rock paintings in the Ennedi Massif. And the wildlife slowly returning in the national parks. I checked a map and see Lake Chad is bounded by 4 countires: Niger, Nigeria, Chad itself and Cameroon. Very interesting video.

replies.author: @PlanetVista4K
replies.text: Beautifully put — the herder and the farmer really is one of the oldest stories there is, and Chad still lives right on that line. And yes, the Bodélé Depression in the north is one of the biggest single sources of the dust that ends up fertilising the Amazon. As for the future, a lot depends on how the rains shift across the Sahel.
